intended_object: The linear part f₁ : M → N of a morphism of right A∞-modules f = (f_n)_{n≥1}, i.e. its arity-one Taylor component, the one with no algebra inputs (Keller, Section 4). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The definition composes the Taylor map `f.taylor : M ⊗ T(sA) → N` with `x ↦ x ⊗ 1`. Here `1` is the empty word, the unit of the tensor-word coalgebra. That gives exactly the component f₁ : M → N. The underlying modules are the same; the suspension only shifts the grading. The lemma `suspendedComponent_zero_tmul_tprod`, proved in the same file, confirms that this agrees with the component with zero algebra inputs. The lemma `barMap_tmul_one` shows it is the map that the bar-construction morphism induces on the counit part, as expected. The setting is general: any commutative ring R and any modules over it. Mathlib has no A∞-modules, so there is no counterpart there.
